name: Kubernetes Patterns
description: Kubernetes — resource limits, liveness/readiness probes, ConfigMaps, namespaces, rolling updates
content:
# Kubernetes Patterns

- Always set resource requests and limits (`cpu`, `memory`) on every container — prevents noisy-neighbor problems and enables proper scheduling
- Configure liveness probes to detect deadlocked containers and readiness probes to control traffic routing — use appropriate endpoints and timeouts
- Store configuration in ConfigMaps and secrets in Secrets — mount them as environment variables or volumes, never bake config into images
- Use namespaces to isolate environments (dev, staging, prod) and teams — apply resource quotas and network policies per namespace
- Use rolling update strategy with proper `maxSurge` and `maxUnavailable` settings — ensure zero-downtime deployments
- Define Pod Disruption Budgets (`PodDisruptionBudget`) for critical services — ensures minimum availability during voluntary disruptions like node drains
- Use labels and selectors consistently — follow a labeling convention (app, version, environment, team) for filtering and service discovery
- Run one process per container — use sidecar containers for logging, proxying, or monitoring instead of cramming multiple processes into one container
- Use `Deployment` for stateless workloads and `StatefulSet` for stateful services — choose the right workload type for the use case
- Store Kubernetes manifests in version control and use GitOps tools (Flux, ArgoCD) — never apply manifests manually to production clusters
